entries.summary: WindowsCredentialManagerSecretStoreOptions gains an optional systemRoot, the absolute Windows system directory PowerShell is started from. Omitted, the store reads process.env.SystemRoot once at construction, as before. A systemRoot that is not an absolute path makes the store unavailable (available() is false, operations throw CREDENTIAL_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE) and never falls back to the process environment; scope() passes it to the scoped store. A Host test that injects platform: "win32" on another OS can pass systemRoot instead of setting the process environment. No Host code change is needed otherwise.

K8 history rows from an external history authority can carry an optional reply, the reply text that the user saw for that Turn (#1318). K8 puts it in the frozen ContextPack row, counts it in contextMaxBytes with the rest of the row (whole rows go oldest first, a reply is never cut) and covers it in historyDigest; K8 still stores no reply text. A reply that is not a string refuses the whole history and the Turn stays queued. historyRowFromTurn in src/rules/context.ts builds a row from a bot-turn:<id> projection value and the reply. Rows without reply behave as before; a Host that vendored K8 copies the new rules/context.ts. K8 also gains the owner call cancelHostIntent(key) (#1320), which cancels a Host intent through K4 and returns cancelled, cancel_pending or already_settled, and throws HostIntentError with unknown_intent or not_host_intent; a Host that called bot.core.cancel on a Host intent key calls cancelHostIntent instead.
